diagram_math_checks.result: [t] is placed at angle 360t degrees, counterclockwise from [0] at the right. The supplier def-circle-as-real-line-mod-integers identifies t and t+n, exactly matching a full turn. The ambient dashed circles carry no additional set-membership assertion.

The Given interval (-1/8,5/8) converts to (-45,225) degrees. The cyan counterclockwise arc is 270 degrees and its two hollow endpoints are excluded. Its length in t is 3/4, so the local open-quotient-arcs supplier gives the open embedded arc used in step 1.1.

The Given interval (3/8,9/8) converts to (135,405) degrees, again a 270-degree open arc. Its endpoint 405 degrees is 45 degrees modulo a full turn. The missing sector of U is contained in V and the missing sector of V is contained in U, including their excluded endpoints; hence the panels illustrate U union V = Q as in step 1.1.

The right arc (-45,45) degrees represents p((-1/8,1/8)) = C. The left arc (135,225) represents p((3/8,5/8)). Their four endpoints are excluded, the remaining sectors separate them, and no additional segment joins them. This is precisely the disjoint decomposition in step 1.1.

The solid rightmost point [0] belongs to U and V and to C in the overlap panel. No point of the left component is identified with [0]. The diagram asserts no extra pushout or fundamental-group relation: steps 2.1–4.1 retain the independent trivial-arc-group, trivial-pushout and nontrivial-circle-group argument, using the unchanged actual local suppliers.
